sources.title: Joo-Yup Lee: The Kazakh Khanate (2019)
sources.note: Author-uploaded full Oxford Research Encyclopedia article directly read, DOI 10.1093/acrefore/9780190277727.013.60. Pages 1,3,7,9: formation, regional scale, juz and disputed formation date. Do not repeat exaggerated troop counts, exact foundation year or all imperial allegiance dates. Canonical publisher mirror counted as same work.

sources.title: Qazaqstan Tarihy: Kazakh Khanate in the XVI century
sources.note: Direct state history portal article: Kasym expansion, decentralization, Hak-Nazar recovery and 1598 campaign/settlement. No population total or exact disputed regnal dates used.

sources.title: Orazgul Muhatova: The way of living of the inhabitants of the Kazakh Khanate (2013)
sources.note: Direct journal metadata plus complete downloaded original Russian PDF, pp85 to 94. Uses broad pastoral seasons p86 and explicitly early-sixteenth-century Ruzbihan reports pp89,91 to 92. Avoids projecting nineteenth/twentieth-century ethnographic detail in same article backward, including one-hour yurt assembly, late food lists and fixed gender roles.

sources.title: Bakhyt Ezhenkhan-uli: Letters from Kazakh khan-sultans to Qing officials concerning trade in Kashgaria (2021)
sources.note: Shygys3/2021, printed44 onward, full institutional PDF downloaded and text read. Printed49 to 50 Abulfeiz1772 letter rice/flour;51 to 52 fabrics1773, white cotton uses and red marital textiles. Modern explanatory ethnography distinguished from dated archival demand. File locally named medicine.pdf but article used is trade, not medicine.

sources.title: Erbulat Smagulov: Sauran Medieval Archaeological Complex in South Kazakhstan (2008)
sources.note: Primary archaeologist article, full indexed original text read via exact URL search; direct fetch timed out/certificate mismatch. Kariz field/garden water, aerial photographs, geological survey and separation of Mirtobe/Sauran systems. Omits conjectural total tunnel lengths and alleged exact source of Mir-Arab works.

sources.title: Sauran madrasa excavations: 2006 field season
sources.note: Original institutional expedition report read in full indexed text; direct fetch unavailable. Concluding plan:31.5x28m, two minarets, courtyard, hujras and darskhana; identification with Wasifi building dated1515. Foundation explicitly predates map and Kazakh takeover.

sources.title: Erbulat Smagulov: The ensemble of the central square of Sauran, fourteenth to sixteenth centuries (2016)
sources.note: Primary excavation paper, Povolzhskaya Arkheologiya2(16),pp93 to 119. Indexed original printed112 verified with query site:archtat.ru/content/uploads/2019/12/2-2016.pdf худжры. Rooms, niches, brick floors and later stove/flue adaptations. Full download failed certificate validation; do not claim entire issue read.

sources.title: Noda Jin and Onuma Takahiro: A Collection of Documents from the Kazakh Sultans to the Qing Dynasty (2010)
sources.note: University of Tokyo TIAS scholarly edition, complete public PDF downloaded. DocumentC printed22 to 24/PDF29 to 31: Abulfeyz1769 Turki letter, JMLZ2339.15,86:3364. Printed22 visually rendered/checked. Line3 تيم قوانديم; modern normalized Arabic-script sample تيم قوانديم, transcription tim quwandïm and translation I was rather pleased on23. Printed6 to 8 bilingual correspondence and envoys.

sources.title: Beibit Yu. Shangirbayeva: The traditional Kazakh bi institution
sources.note: Direct academic chapter, traditional judiciary and customary law sections. Author explicitly presents an ideal model partly reconstructed from nineteenth-century sources; retains that limitation. No unsourced thirteen-year-old judge story or blanket fairness/equality claim.

sources.title: Onuma Takahiro: The shift in Qing-Kazakh relations, the Qing western territory in the 1770s
sources.note: Complete downloaded primary archival study, Memoirs of the Toyo Bunko76(2018),pp35 to 56. Printed35 to 38 political formula,1775 requested troops, refusal and diplomatic friction. Filename2019 differs from printed journal date2018.

sources.title: Z. E. Kabuldinov: The abolition of khan power in Kazakhstan (2018)
sources.note: Full Institute of History journal downloaded; printed51 onward, especially54 oath1731,58 to 61 administration1822/1824. Ending describes regional institutional abolition, not disappearance of Kazakh people or instant nationwide annexation.

proposedOverrides.summary: A major Kazakh steppe power with pastoral communities, southern towns and changing regional khans; the imported dates show only part of its history.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Exact indexed ID and five decoded imported snapshots1530 to 1783 verified in identities.json. Missing runtime card/override and no staged packet collision at claim. Broad steppe bbox57.15 to 87.09E/40.92 to 55.31N is not a modern national border or proof of uniform territorial control. Fifteenth-century formation and later institutional abolition are public. No aliases; preserve any subsequently curated fell/successors. School1515 and early16thtravel descriptions explicitly predate map1530. No unsupported toilets or medical practice added.
